symptom: Under `mdl 1;` a log / show message / validation feedback template holding a line break had no spelling as template text: `'a\nb'` is a backslash and an n, and a literal with the break in it became the template `{1}` with the literal as its parameter. `describe` inside an mdl 1 script printed `\n`, so describe -> exec under the header rewrote every Studio Pro template ending in a line break (PedApp VAL_Feedback, TestApp WorkflowCommons). With `with ({n} = …)` parameters the same literal wrote its quotes into a log's template text and shifted a message's parameters one place under both versions.
cause: The builders took the template text only from a bare `*ast.LiteralExpr`; buildSourceExpression wraps any expression whose source spans lines in `*ast.SourceExpr` (stored as written), so a multi-line literal fell to the `{1}` branch. The describer quoted template text with mdl 0's mdlQuote regardless of describeLanguage.
fix: A lone string literal as a template message is unwrapped to its LiteralExpr under mdl 1 (and under both versions when the statement has template parameters); under mdl 0 the lone multi-line case warns MDL-V1-TEMPLATE with an upgrade rewrite to `'{1}' with ({1} = <literal>)`. escapeFix now rewrites an escaped line break in a template literal. describe under mdl 1 quotes template text with `''` only.
insight: 'Stored as written' is decided by the expression's SHAPE (spans lines), not its position, so any slot that treats a literal specially must look through SourceExpr. describe under mdl 1 still writes mdl 0 escapes for every other string (annotations with \r\n made TestApp's ASU_UserTaskView_Migrate refuse the splice) — that is the same class, left to its own change. Revert checks: templateQuote -> mdlQuote fails the PedApp/TestApp round trip at describe; buildTemplateMessage -> buildSourceExpression makes exec under mdl 1 write the flow.
